label: trisyncolpate
reason: Correct: syncolpate means the colpi meet (fuse) at the poles; PATO has no aperture terms. Structure is an acceptable parent, like the other pollen and leaf-division structure values.

label: triternate
reason: Standard meaning (thrice ternate); same form and parent as its sibling FLOPO:0991241 biternate; PATO has no ternate terms.

label: sordid
reason: Glossaries give sordid as dull, dingy, dirty-looking, usually of a whitish colour; PATO has no such colour value. 'dirty white' fits the usual floristic use.

label: sausage-shaped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongate and cylindrical with rounded ends, straight or slightly curved, like a sausage.
reason: Meaning and synonym allantoid are right, but a curved sausage (the usual sense of allantoid) is not a convex body, so convex 3-D shape (PATO:0002007) is the wrong parent. Move it to shape (PATO:0000052).

label: evenly spaced
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being separated from the neighbouring structures of its kind by about equal distances.
reason: Meaning right, and PATO has no such value, but the text names 'a set of structures' as the bearer and does not follow the 'by virtue of the bearer's' form. Rewritten so the quality inheres in each member, as with PATO:0001952 distichous.

label: multistemmed
reason: Correct habit term (several stems from or near the base, no single trunk); branched is a reasonable parent and PATO has no such term.

label: tubercle-based
reason: Correct: a hair arising from an enlarged, wart-like multicellular base (pustulate-based). It inheres in the trichome, and the note already records that the stated stem or leaf is the whole the trichome belongs to.

label: camptodromous
definition: A pinnately veined quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's secondary veins not ending at the margin but curving upwards before it, either fading out or joining the secondary vein above.
reason: In Hickey (1973) camptodromous covers all pinnate venation whose secondary veins do not reach the margin, including brochidodromous (joined in loops) and eucamptodromous. 'curving upwards near it' alone is too narrow. PATO:0001970 brochidodromous should then sit under this class.

label: polystichous
reason: Correct (arranged in many ranks); same parent as its sibling PATO:0001952 distichous; multifarious and many-ranked are standard synonyms.

label: intravaginal
reason: Correct grass and sedge innovation term; the exact counterpart of FLOPO:0991357 extravaginal, with the same parent.

label: stomatomorphic
reason: Fits the literal sense (stoma-shaped: two lips around a slit) and is limited to stigmas, as the source uses it. I could not confirm a standard glossary definition, so confidence is low.

label: gelatinous
reason: Correct; PATO has no gelatinous texture value (viscous is a viscosity value, and glutinous in PATO is an amylose composition). A French synonym follows earlier rows (e.g. biterné).

label: latrorse
reason: Correct, worded the same way as its siblings FLOPO:0991164 introrse and FLOPO:0991165 extrorse.

label: holomycotrophic
reason: Overlaps FLOPO:0991360 saprophytic, which already has the exact synonym 'mycoheterotrophic' and describes the same achlorophyllous, fungus-fed plants that floras call saprophytic. Two classes would split one set of annotations. Either merge them, or keep holomycotrophic as the correct term and make saprophytic a synonym or a deprecated class pointing to it.

label: semi-ellipsoid
reason: Correct and well formed; a half ellipsoid is convex, so the parent fits. PATO has ellipsoid but no half form.

label: upper
reason: Correct for a member's place in its series ('upper leaves'); PATO has only relational terms (distal to), which do not fit the 'state of the bearer' pattern.

label: lower
reason: Exact counterpart of upper; correct and well formed.

label: inner
reason: Correct for whorls and series ('inner tepals', 'inner bracts' of an involucre); well formed.

label: outer
reason: Exact counterpart of inner; correct and well formed.

label: lateral (sensu botany)
reason: The definition is right for a member of a series (lateral sepals or petals, as in orchids), but the related synonym 'lateral' will also match 'lateral inflorescences, buds, branches or veins', where lateral means arising from the side of an axis (axillary, not terminal). That is a second meaning. Match only on the series words (sepal, petal, tepal, lobe), or send 'lateral' + axis parts to FLOPO:0991000 axillary or PATO:0001193 lateral to.

label: median
reason: Synonyms do not fit. In floras, 'middle' (1,574 statements) mostly means midway along an axis ('middle cauline leaves', between upper and lower), not the median member between lateral ones. 'central' overlaps inner (FLOPO:0991378). FLOPO:0991299 medial (sensu botany) already has 'median' as a related synonym with another meaning. Either give 'middle' its own class (midway between the upper and lower members) or drop it, and remove 'median' from FLOPO:0991299.

label: porrect
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's projecting straight outwards from the surface or axis that bears it, neither ascending nor bent back or down.
reason: Glossaries give porrect as directed outward and forward, extended straight out. 'at about a right angle' clashes with its own synonym 'projecting forward' and is stricter than flora usage, where porrect spines are contrasted with ascending, spreading and descending ones.

label: obliquely truncate
reason: Correct child of PATO:0000936 truncated (the Carex perigynium beak orifice); well formed.

label: candelabriform
reason: Correct habit term (branches curving out and then erect, as in candelabra euphorbias and cacti); branched is the right parent.

label: epicortical
reason: Correct for the epicortical roots of mistletoes (Loranthaceae and Viscaceae), which run over the host bark and send haustoria into it; positional parent fits, like its siblings aerial and subterranean.
